text: K-NN K-NN is the most simple supervised learning algorithm. First, the model is trained using training data [30]. K-NN then predicts the outcome of the test data by using a similarity measure w.r.t. the trained data. K stands for the number of neighbours. Mostly Euclidean distance is employed to determine the distance between the samples. K is a crucial parameter which must be selected consciously as it is important to strike a bal- ance between underfitting and overfitting. 7.2  Cross‑validation The traditional train split model divides/dissects the data randomly into training data and testing data. Mostly, the training set consists of 80% data and testing is performed on the rest 20%. It is generally used on larger datasets where training is required only once. How- ever, the major limitation of traditional splitting is that the random splitting of data leads to variations in performance accuracy. Also, it fails badly/poorly for datasets which are evenly distributed as it may result in diversity in training and testing sets. Shortcomings of the traditional train split model can be managed by K fold cv [42]. In this, a k value is chosen as per the requirement which serves as the number of folds. The dataset is then divided into k equal folds. The training set comprises (k-1) folds and the last fold is used for the testing phase. Then the model is trained. This process is repeated till each fold is used for testing exactly once. In this work, a tenfold cv has been utilized. In tenfold cv the dataset has been divided randomly into 10 equal subsets [4]. In each fold, 9 subsets are utilized for training and one for testing. As the number of folds has been chosen as 10, the experiment has been performed 10 times where each subset is used for testing exactly once. 7.3  Performance evaluation measures The validation of the ML-based proposed system has been conducted via performance evaluation measures i.e. Accuracy (ACC), Sensitivity (SENS) and Specificity (SPEC) These can be computed by using follows equations: Eqs.
